newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares recoup early losses, edge higher.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares recoup early losses, edge higher.

text.p: The Athens bourse emerged weaker after Monday's strong 2.74 percent rebound but managed to recoup early losses and settle with mild gains as the benchmark share index climbed 0.25 percent on turnover of 5.4 billion drachmas.

"After the recent panic selling we had a logical upside reaction. There is a flight to quality but in time this can encompass secondary stocks and lead to a sustained recovery," said Nick Verras, director of private banking at Interbank.

"Many stocks were hammered and the mindset these days is how to benefit from the run up which seems to have more to go. The strategy calls for cautious buying of quality shares with proven earnings power," he said.
It was the fourth normal session since a settlement scandal halted trading for almost four days.
On Monday brokers association president resolved a disagreement over a draft bill on the exchange after meeting with National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou.
Verras said the upcoming tax on interest earned on state debt paper and lower rate cuts were boosting the case for equities.
But institutional changes allowing pension funds to invest in stocks would be the catalyst for a bull market if the government delivers on recent promises.
"Pension funds are not cyclical institutional players. They have a steady stream of funds which they can direct to the equities market," he said.

The Athens general share index closed up 0.25 percent or 2.28 points higher at 917.10 from Monday's 914.82 close after opening at 915.08. Turnover was 5.45 billion drachmas after on volume of 2.8 million shares.
